item.title: That Stupid Pelican On A Bicycle
item.description:
Today I will show you something remarkable.

All the documented and controlled “experiments” which performed controlled comparisons of the LLMs with that degenerate pelican-on-a-bicycle meme “test” produced the result of that fucking pelican facing right – 100%, without a single exception.

Here is a claim, which cannot be imperically verified but can be easily justified from the first principles unudertanding – every major model for the very same prompt (without a single word altered) will produce the image of a pelicane facing right.

item.title: The sheer idiocy of building "small" multimodal models
item.description:
The striking idiocy of keeping making multimodal “local” models to fit into the intentionally (to maximize profits) memory-limited crapbooks of the Mac cult victims, is beyond my comprehension.

Yes, nothing local runs on an over-priced 16GB crapbooks, and barely runs (~ 1 token/sec) on 32GB crippled Mac Minies, since there are no mainstream Macbooks with 32GB and the top-tier Pro models cost like $3K+.

To fullfill the demand of the igorant cultists all kinds of Q4_0 crappy factorizations are being built, which produce a very generic, commonplace slop for reasons discussed at length here.

item.title: The One-shot Result
item.description:
Recently there were lots of nonsense posted on Xitter and elsewhere about “complete AA-grade games " or “ready to production CAD designs” from a single simplistic prompts, like “make me an AA grade first person shooter with photo-realistic graphics”, almost literally.

The question, of course, is not how it dances so well, but how it dances at all.

The answer seems to be “the training process and the training data”, as usual.

item.title: On Crapto
item.description:
I am an Alexander Elder’s fan and student, not just because I am a refugee too (my mom is Ukrainian), but because he essentially figured it all out back in the hecking 1993, before trading even became mainstream, and his system withstood the test of more than 25 years and completely, totally different, fully automated markets.

I am also a big fan of the Jane Street “cool story”, at least the part that they shill to the public and which I understand quite well – a man studied at a very good school (Cornell), with the right tradition (ML-family) under the best teachers (Clarkson and Co.), got a PhD (which means got the Right Understanding and proper Indoctrination) and then used the Ocaml language (designed and implemented by correctness-obsessed serious theoreticians and academics) for semi-automation of error-prone tasks, with not just significant, but very large (potentially destructive) costs of errors.

item.title: The Mother Of All Bubbles
item.description:
Yes, yes, a fresh, young p***y popped the AI bubble. Nothing is new under the moon.

Anyway, let’s see what we have at this auspicious moment. It is time to say farewell to the AI hype and the bubble caused by it (and yes, we will “say goodbye” many more times, for sure, because it won’t leave for good).

The Fundamental Problem is still Out There and cannot (and won’t) be solved – the slop generator, however large, does not posses any “knowledge”, “understanding” or “reasoning” of any kind.

item.title: Where We Are So Far
item.description:
So, this is what is actually going on (seen as they are) in plain English.

The sheer brute-force of data-center-sized “frontier” models is so brute that it easily appears as “intelligence”.

This is still the next-token prediction based on a conditional probability under the hood.

There is no “understanding”, no “reasoning”, no “knowledge”, no “skills” (these are just the same streams of tokens).

But this is not mere a “glorified autocomplete” anymore. There are compilers, code linters and even basic static analysis tools in the loop.

item.title: Monads, yes, again
item.description:
People are saying avoid Monad “tutorials” [written by unqualified retards] , so writing down one is an IQ test and understanding is a “filter”.

And, indeed, one has to know and understand some related concepts and become to a certain kind of mathematical thinking, otherwise one would apply bullshit imperative programming concepts instead of mathematical ones.

The first concept is “composition of functions”, the famous \(\circ\) operator of the traditional mathematical notation. it takes two functions (of a single argument) and produces a new function (of a single argument, which is operationally defined is nesting of function calls.
